title: Competing-hypothesis / counter-evidence case: app redesign, doubled ad spend and a competitor outage in the same month

input.researchQuestion: Did the May 2025 app redesign raise the conversion rate?

datasets.description: Fictional conversions per 10,000 sessions before and after the redesign.
Fictional trade-press article reporting a week-long outage at the main competitor in May 2025, with a link to the competitor's own status page.

expectations.text: The redesign brief (April 2025) predicted conversions per 10k sessions would rise by about 30 after launch.

hypotheses.text: Doubled ad spend brought higher-intent traffic.
A competitor outage diverted ready-to-buy customers.

evidence.summary: Conversions rose from 200 to 260 per 10k sessions, above the +30 predicted.
Ad spend doubled in the same month, so the rise cannot be attributed to the redesign alone.
Spend index 100 to 200 coincides with the conversion jump.
Trade-press report of the competitor outage, traceable to the competitor's status page.

requiredLimitations: Three candidate causes changed in the same month; the design cannot separate them.
The prior expectation being met does not rule out the competing explanations.
The competitor outage is reported by a third party and its traffic effect is not measured.

requiredResearchGaps.need: Conversion split by traffic source (paid vs organic) for April and May.
Daily conversions around the redesign launch date and the outage window.
Referral traffic from the competitor's domain during the outage.

forbiddenClaims: リデザインによってコンバージョンが向上した
リデザインの効果が証明

humanReview.notes: A passing report keeps all three hypotheses open and names the traffic-source split as the next data.
